..
A trade-wind trough from the east made its approach today, bringing 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across the Marianas. The
heaviest of showers is occurring over the CNMI, significantly 
shearing off near Guam. Shower activity will continue through Sunday,
but will downtrend after tonight. As of now, thunderstorm potential 
looks to be little to none based on drier air aloft continuing to cap
any vertical growth, but this will be monitored overnight. Based on 
latest satellite imagery, shower activity may not even last through 
Sunday morning, but a surge in moisture upstream of the trough should
allow showers to linger. Beginning Sunday night, isolated showers 
will return to the region throughout the rest of the forecast period.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Guam is abnormally dry (D0)
and the CNMI remains unchanged. Hopefully, rainfall tonight can
bring temporary relief, but drought conditions may continue and 
possibly worsen afterwards as the dry season approaches. Water 
conservation is encouraged over the next several weeks.

Marine/Surf...
Moderate trade winds will prevail through Thursday, possibly 
increasing up to low-end fresh on Tuesday and Wednesday. Combined 
seas are down-trending and expected to be 5 to 7 feet tonight. Seas 
are comprised of a diminishing north swell and a trade swell. Seas 
will continue to subside over the next few days but may increase back
to 6 to 8 feet around the middle of next week as the trade swell 
builds.

Surf observations today reported surf of 4 to 7 feet along north-
facing reefs. As such, the elevated, long-period north swell has 
subsided enough for surf to fall below hazardous criteria of 9 feet,
so the High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current Risk Statement for
north-facing reefs expired this afternoon. However, surf along 
north- and east-facing reefs will remain elevated at 6 to 8 feet at 
least through Sunday. This will produce a moderate risk of rip 
currents along all reefs over the next several days. When in doubt, 
don't go out.

Eastern Micronesia...
Drier weather is expected to prevail on Sunday with only isolated 
showers expected at all forecast points. Low-end scattered showers 
will be possible at Pohnpei and possibly at Majuro starting Sunday 
night with a trough approaching Pohnpei from the east and the 
remnants of Tropical Storm Pena moving north of Majuro through 
Monday. Scattered shower chances will continue at Majuro and Pohnpei 
through Monday. The circulation associated with the remnants of Pena 
will open into a trough late on Sunday as it continues to traverse 
the eastern portions of Micronesia. With that said, some scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms will be possible starting Sunday 
and continuing through early next week for portions of the northern 
RMI. Drier weather is expected to persist at Kosrae through early 
next week. A series of trade-wind troughs may bring scattered showers
for all forecast locations starting Wednesday with some higher-end 
scattered showers possible Friday and into the weekend. Confidence is
not all that high in the extended portion of the forecast, but model
guidance continues to suggest some wet weather may be in store for 
late next week and into the weekend, stay tuned! Light to gentle 
winds will persist through at least midweek at all forecast points 
with the possibility of gentle to moderate developing at Majuro late 
next week. Combined seas of 4 to 7 feet will generally prevail at all
forecast sites through tonight with seas dropping a foot or so 
starting on Sunday. Seas consist of a northeast, a north-northwest, 
and a small, southeast swell.

Most of eastern Micronesia is experiencing abnormally dry (D0) 
drought conditions. Try to conserve water as we continue to
transition into the dry season.

Western Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) is now back in place across western
Micronesia, though it is pretty weak at this time. Latest satellite
data does show low-end scattered showers currently in Palau waters,
decreasing over the past few hours. This trend will continue, with 
showers becoming isolated no later than midnight. then Palau will 
join Yap with a dry trade-wind pattern seen over the area through the
beginning of next week. Chuuk will remain dry through the remainder 
of the weekend. By Monday, the NET looks to become a bit more active,
with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms moving into Chuuk,
then spreading west into Yap and Palau. Unfortunately, rainfall 
amounts don't look to be too impressive, so residents of Yap, Palau 
and Chuuk should continue to follow their prescribed method of 
preserving water.

The north swell is slowly subsiding and looks to fall sufficiently
for surf to fall below hazardous levels Sunday afternoon. Surf will
remain a bit elevated through at least Monday, but should be around 
8 feet or less. Gentle to moderate trade winds will continue through
the middle of next week.
